blocks.x: Care management succeeds on precision targeting and timely intervention: identifying rising-risk members, coordinating across providers, and proving quality outcomes. It is a data-discipline business, and the data discipline is usually the missing part. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in risk stratification, care outreach and scheduling, program matching, with quality measure reporting close behind. Volume grows on every path; the decision layer has not kept up. That gap is measurable, and it is the work.
Care Management & Population Health: the recurring pressure points,

items: Claims, clinical, SDOH and engagement data siloed; risk stratification runs on claims only.
Care outreach, scheduling and follow-up run on call lists; gaps between contacts lose members.
Members matched to programs by blunt rules; engagement economics unmeasured.
Care teams share sensitive data across vendors; controls lag.
HEDIS-class measures assembled manually per cycle; evidence assembled under deadline.
Care platforms integrate by file export; workflows break at handoffs.

blocks.x: The proof in Care Management & Population Health is a working system on a real workflow. These are the builds that go live:

items: claims/clinical/SDOH unified with certified risk features
contact plans executed across channels with follow-up policy
engagement likelihood + clinical need into assignment
event-driven care workflows replacing file exports
